dynamic sitting has no effect on low back pain or low back discomfort.
dynamic sitting approaches do not have a significant effect on LBP or low back discomfort.

the development of a novel, non-invasive, wearable device for the prevention and treatment of low back pain (and other musculoskeletal disorders) in the workplace and home.
the development of new methods to prevent and manage low back pain ( LBP ).
the development of a novel approach to the design of dynamic sitting chairs, which we call ‘dynamic sitting’ (DS).

there is no evidence to support dynamic sitting as a management approach for LBD and LBP.

dynamic sitting approaches may be effective as an adjunctive management approach to other interventions for subjects with LBP.
